title: third-party-accelerator-onboarding-and-runtime-integration-2026
author: Aisha Kumar
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the engineering process, interface contracts, testing checklist, performance profiling playbook, and runbook steps required to safely onboard third-party accelerator kernels (vendor-provided or community plugins) into Redwood's serving runtime. It is intended for runtime engineers, kernel maintainers, release engineers, and partners delivering binary kernels.

Scope: Includes ABI/handshake, scheduling delegation, telemetry requirements, automated benchmarks, release gating criteria, and emergency rollback procedures. Does NOT cover dedicated/hardware procurement policies or vendor commercial agreements.

Key goals
- Protect production SLOs (p95 latency, p99 tail, and throughput) when new kernels are introduced.
- Ensure predictable fallbacks and fast mitigation for regressions.
- Provide a repeatable onboarding checklist for partner kernels.
- Integrate kernel-level telemetry into profiler and benchmark suites.

1) Architecture and contracts
1.1 High-level flow
- Client request -> Router -> Kernel-aware Scheduler -> Accelerator Driver -> Kernel Binary -> Execution -> KV Cache / Memory Manager -> Response
- The scheduler exposes a lightweight delegation API to accept or decline work based on kernel-reported capacity hints.

1.2 Required contracts (must be implemented by any third-party kernel)
- ABI handshake: JSON manifest exchanged at registration time containing: kernel_id, supported-ops, max_sequence_length, preferred_batch_shape, memory_reservation_bytes, suggested_concurrency, quantization_support (none/int8/fp16), version, and signature (SHA256).
- Health API: /kernel/health -> { status: ready|degraded|unavailable, current_load: int, available_slots: int } (gRPC or HTTP as configured).
- Telemetry hooks: emit tracing span with tag kernel.id, provide per-call token_count and per-buffer memory_usage metrics.
- Fallback hints: on degradation kernel must supply a suggested fallback model_variant or indicate graceful-degradation behavior.

2) Scheduling & delegation model
- Scheduler roles: admission control, prioritization, and preemption signaling.
- Delegation handshake: scheduler sends a PROBE (100–200ms budget) to allow kernel to confirm readiness and advertise capacity. If no response within the probe window, scheduler treats kernel as unavailable for that allocation.
- Priority mapping: requests carry route_priority (0=system,1=premium,2=default,3=best-effort). Kernel must accept or reject based on a priority bitmap advertised in the manifest.
- Preemption signal: scheduler may send PREEMPT_WITH_INTENT to request graceful early termination of lower-priority in-flight work. Kernels must support checkpointing of KV cache state if execution spans >500ms.

3) Profiling playbook for new kernels
- Baseline collection steps (automated pipeline)
  1. Deploy kernel in isolated sandbox cluster with synthetic traffic that mirrors target route shapes (short-form-chat, long-sequence-completion, embeddings).
  2. Run 3 x 30-minute runs per workload shape at steady concurrency targets: low (10%), nominal (100%), and burst (300%).
  3. Capture full traces, kernel internal counters, GPU occupancy, PCIe/NVLink bandwidth, host CPU steal, and memory fragmentation metrics.
- Key signals to evaluate
  - mean_token_latency, p95/p99 token generation latency, kernel_dispatch_time, kernel_queue_wait, kernel_compute_time, kvcache_hit_ratio, memory_alloc_failures.
  - cost proxy: tokens/sec per accelerator-hour and estimated $/1M tokens using current price model.
- Failure modes to flag automatically
  - sudden increase (>20%) in p99 with no corresponding CPU or request-shape delta.
  - unbounded growth in memory ( > 5% per minute over 5 minutes).
  - frequent short bumps in kernel_queue_wait correlated with NVLink retransmits.

4) Benchmarking suite integration steps
- Add kernel to perf-registry: a YAML entry in the benchmarking repo with fields: kernel_id, node_type, driver_version, regression_thresholds. Example table:
| field | example | description |
| kernel_id | vendorX-int8-v2 | unique id used in manifests |
| node_type | g10x-48GB | validated hardware profile |
| driver_version | 4.2.1 | expected driver / runtime combo |
| p99_threshold_ms | 42 | absolute gating p99 for nominal workload |
| throughput_tokens_per_sec | 12_000 | expected steady-state throughput |

- Bench harness requirements
  - Must run the kernel under the same batching and prefix-caching configs used in production.
  - Mirror request provenance (token lengths, system prompts, function call patterns).
  - Produce an artifact: annotated trace (.zip) plus a normalized perf JSON that includes histograms.

5) Release gating and validation
- Mandatory checks (all must pass for canary rollout)
  1. Unit trust: manifest signature verified and integration tests pass (functional correctness).
  2. Canary perf: benchmark harness p99 and throughput within 95% of golden baseline.
  3. Telemetry conformity: kernel emits required spans and metrics.
  4. Graceful-fallback test: simulated node failure triggers scheduler fallback without client error rate > 0.1%.
- Progressive rollout plan
  1. Sandbox -> internal canary (5% infra) for 24h -> expanded canary (25%) for 72h -> production (100%) with 2-week monitoring holds.
  2. Automatic rollback if: p99 increases by >25% or error rate increases by >0.5% over baseline within the observation window.

6) Known issues and mitigation patterns (for this kernel onboarding flow)
- Issue: kernel reports low available_slots intermittently causing oscillation. Mitigation: enable probe backoff to 2s and increase scheduler probe timeout for the node pool.
- Issue: memory fragmentation leads to OOM on long sequences. Mitigation: enable slab compaction on host and tune kernel memory_reservation_bytes in manifest.
- Issue: degraded telemetry fidelity (missing token_count). Mitigation: fail the canary and require kernel debug build with logging enabled; add temporary sidecar to enrich traces.

7) Runbook: emergency rollback (fast path)
- Preconditions: alert fires for rolling-p99-regression OR >0.2% client errors for >5 minutes.
- Fast rollback steps (under 15 minutes target)
  1. Runbook initiator (oncall) adds "kernel-quarantine" tag to affected node group in cluster manager.
  2. Drain new kernel variant from router by toggling route-level kernel preference to previous kernel_id via feature toggle service.
  3. Trigger scheduler-level evict-and-failover: call /scheduler/evict?kernel_id=<id>&grace=30s on impacted pool.
  4. Revert driver-level configuration if driver update applied within last 6h.
  5. Roll forward mitigation: re-run perf smoke tests on a mirrored sandbox; if passes, perform controlled reintroduce at 5% for 2 hours.
  6. Document incident in postmortem with timeline, traces, and kernels artifacts.

Checklist quick-reference (for on-call)
- [ ] Is the manifest signature valid?
- [ ] Are health pings returning `ready` from all nodes?
- [ ] Is p99 > baseline by threshold? (check dashboard)
- [ ] Apply kernel-quarantine tag if failing
- [ ] Start rollback sequence and notify ops@redwood.com

8) Ownership & contacts
- Primary owner: eng-serving-runtime (runtime-kernel-onboarding squad)
- Secondary owners: infra-release, eng-platform-observability
- Pager escalation: runtime-oncall -> kernel-oncall -> eng-platform SRE lead
- Documentation owner: Aisha Kumar

9) Appendix: sample manifest (stringified)
| key | example | notes |
|-----------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| kernel_id | vendorx/gemm-int8-2026-04 | must be globally unique within perf registry |
| supported_ops | ["matmul","attention","layernorm"] | operator subset; runtime will reject ops not listed |
| preferred_batch_shape | [1, 8, 2048] | suggested batch shapes for best throughput |
| memory_reservation_bytes | 40000000000 | reserve 40GB to avoid fragmentation |
| telemetry_version | 1.1 | matches runtime tracer contract |

CLI snippets
- Register kernel manifest: redwoodctl kernel register --manifest=vendorx-manifest.json --pool=canary-pool
- Run benchmark: redwood-bench run --kernel=vendorx/gemm-int8-2026-04 --profile=long-seq --output=artifacts/vendorx.zip
- Quarantine pool: redwoodctl pool tag add --pool=canary-pool --tag=kernel-quarantine

Change log / release notes (template)
- 2026-03-01: Initial draft and checklist published (Aisha Kumar)
- 2026-03-10: Updated profiling thresholds and added emergency rollback steps (reviewers: Miguel Santos, Priya Nair)

Related artifacts
- Benchmarking repo: git@internal:redwood/serving-benchmarks.git (perf-registry / kernel-entries)
- Telemetry schema: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/team-wiki/runtime-telemetry-sampling-cost-aware-profiling-2027 (see event schema v1.1)

Notes and next steps
- Short-term: automate manifest signature checks as a pre-commit hook in the perf-registry.
- Mid-term: build a simulator that replays scheduler-probe patterns to detect oscillations before canary.
- Long-term: extend ABI to support multi-accel fused kernels and dynamic quantization negotiation.

End of document
